claim: On a consumer-GPU MoE deployment with no P2P, inter-GPU communication accounts for 81.6% of total execution time on RTX 5090, and naive deployment reaches only 61% of the throughput of a FLOP-matched datacenter GPU.
stance_target: the repo's premise that the fabric, not compute, is the binding constraint for MoE work on this box
scope_conditions: 8x RTX 5090 (PCIe 5.0 x16), BF16, four MoE models 16B-31B, ShareGPT workload
quoted_support: As our benchmarks reveal, this performance collapse is due to the dominant inter-GPU communication cost; on RTX 5090, communication overhead accounts for 81.6% of the total execution time... directly deploying existing MoE inference systems on consumer GPUs yields poor performance (as low as 61% of the throughput compared to datacenter GPUs with similar FLOPs).

claim: PCIe 5.0 x16 gives 64 GB/s nominal inter-GPU bandwidth versus 400 GB/s on NVLink, a ratio of 0.16x, and effective inter-GPU bandwidth is even lower because all traffic is host-mediated.
stance_target: the repo's bandwidth arithmetic comparing PCIe to NVLink
scope_conditions: A800-SXM vs RTX 5090; nominal one-way PCIe capacity
quoted_support: Inter-GPU BW (GB/s) 400 [NVLink] vs 64 [PCIe 5.0 x16], 0.16x... effective bandwidth for inter-GPU communication is even lower due to host mediation.

claim: Treating host DRAM as an active routing hub rather than a passive bounce buffer raises MoE inference throughput on 8x RTX 5090 by 1.24x to 1.41x per model (up to 1.46x), reaching 85-90% of an NVLink A800 + DeepEP configuration at 23.4% of the hardware cost.
stance_target: the claim that host-staged communication is not merely a penalty but a topology that can be exploited, which weakens a blanket 'EP is ruled out' verdict
scope_conditions: 8x RTX 5090 vs 8x A800 (NVLink 400 GB/s); SGLang 0.5.9 baseline; DeepEP v1.2.1 patched for SM80
quoted_support: The results show that on the RTX 5090, CoMoE improves inference throughput by up to 1.46x over SGLang. Moreover, it brings TTFT close to that of an A800 system equipped with high-speed NVLink interconnects and reaches 85-90% of the throughput of the strongest A800 configuration (SGLang with DeepEP). To deliver the same serving throughput as that configuration, CoMoE requires at most 23.4% of the equivalent GPU investment.

claim: Decomposing the All-to-All combine into one-sided token-level transfers through host staging yields a 2.46x geometric-mean speedup over NCCL All-to-All and a 1.59x speedup over the same design without the secondary optimizations, cutting average latency 48.9% and 27.5% respectively.
stance_target: the claim that bulk-synchronous collectives are the wrong primitive for a host-mediated fabric
scope_conditions: DeepSeek-V2-Lite hidden size 2048, 6 experts per token, 1-256 token combine requests
quoted_support: Overall, the full design achieves a 2.46x geometric-mean speedup over NCCL All-to-All and a 1.59x speedup over CoMoE-raw, reducing average latency by 48.9% and 27.5%, respectively.

claim: Removing the global barrier from MoE combine improves throughput by 4.9% to 13.2% depending on model, showing that straggler stalls from dynamic expert load imbalance are a material cost on a host-mediated fabric.
stance_target: the claim that EP's rigid collectives compound the hardware penalty
scope_conditions: 8x RTX 5090; CoMoE vs a CoMoE-Sync variant with an injected global barrier after expert computation
quoted_support: The largest gains appear on Qwen3-30B-A3B and GLM-4.7-Flash, where CoMoE improves throughput over CoMoE-Sync by 13.2% (from 4,865.47 to 5,506.00) and 11.2% (from 3,029.06 to 3,367.13), respectively... even for models with inherently higher baseline performance, such as DeepSeek-V2-Lite and GPT-OSS-20B, CoMoE still delivers 4.9% and 8.1% improvements.

claim: CoMoE reduces TTFT by 18.8% and TPOT by 26.9% on average across four MoE models and all tested request rates, with the largest relative gains under light-to-moderate load where communication dominates.
stance_target: how much of end-to-end latency on this fabric is communication rather than compute
scope_conditions: 8x RTX 5090, 1,000 ShareGPT prompts per model-backend pair, request rates 0-24 req/s
quoted_support: Across all evaluated models and request rates, CoMoE consistently achieves lower latency than the baseline, reducing TTFT by 18.8% and TPOT by 26.9% on average. The relative improvement is largest under light-to-moderate load, where communication overhead dominates end-to-end latency.

claim: Consumer GPUs lack PCIe peer-to-peer support in multi-GPU deployments, so every cross-GPU transfer must traverse the PCIe fabric through host DRAM, consuming host-side bandwidth and synchronization.
scope_conditions: consumer-grade GPUs (RTX 5090 class) in multi-GPU servers
quoted_support: In contrast, consumer GPUs lack support for PCIe peer-to-peer (P2P) communication in multi-GPU deployments. Every cross-GPU transfer must traverse the PCIe fabric... additionally consume host-side bandwidth and synchronization.

claim: Modern fine-grained MoE models use 64 to 128 or more experts per layer, which forces multi-GPU deployment via expert parallelism because the aggregated expert footprint exceeds single-GPU capacity.
stance_target: whether an MoE experiment on 5x64 GB cards can avoid EP entirely by replicating experts
quoted_support: The recent trend of modern MoE towards fine-grained specialization has driven the total expert count significantly higher - typically ranging from 64 to 128 or more (e.g., DeepSeek-v2, Qwen3, and GLM-4.7). Because the aggregated memory footprint of these dozens or hundreds of experts typically exceeds single-GPU capacity, this necessitates multi-GPU deployments via Expert Parallelism (EP).
